title: Pyramids of Sneferu at Dahshur
summary: At Dahshur, south of Memphis, King Sneferu of the Fourth Dynasty built the Bent Pyramid and the Red Pyramid. The Bent Pyramid changed slope partway up; the Red Pyramid is generally regarded as the first successfully completed true pyramid, with smooth sides, and the third largest in Egypt.

uncertainty.note: The range is Sneferu's reign (c. 2613-2589 BC) per the Ministry, not a dated building period; the Red Pyramid's own building is placed by the Ministry at year 13 of the reign plus about 10 years. Magli dates Sneferu around 2575 BC.

reviewer_note: Model is the Red Pyramid only (shape: pyramid, true smooth-sided form), taken from Magli's published figures (104.4 m tall, base 218.5 by 221.5 m); other sources give 104-105 m and about 220 m, and the Ministry pages give no numbers. Construction phase is derived: reign start -2612 + year 13, +10 years. Magli is an arXiv preprint (class scholarly), not a museum or heritage body. Record covers both pyramids but the pin and model are the Red Pyramid.

phases.description: Red Pyramid built over about ten years, begun around year 13 of Sneferu's reign (reign dated c. 2613-2589 BC); the years are derived from those two statements.
Pyramid completed and cased in white Tura limestone; the casing was later reused in medieval times (date not given), leaving the reddish core visible.
